course.title: Full-Stack Web Application Development with Python & Django — Initial cohort draft
course.shortDescription: Six guided classes covering web requests and python data modelling; django applications, models and migrations; forms and server-side validation; rest apis and serializers; authentication and reusable templates; security tests and production operations.
course.description:
A guided course for learners who want to build and explain a working student-management application.

Outcomes

  1. Draw the request lifecycle and write a five-student score program. Calculate the average and highest score, handle an empty dataset and explain your chosen data structures.
  2. Create a students app, dashboard view and Student model. Apply the migration in an isolated database and add three records. Show duplicate student-code rejection and a missing-record response.
  3. Build a name/email/course registration form. Demonstrate invalid email handling, retained values, CSRF protection and a successful redirect. Explain why a student must not be able to submit an administrator flag.
  4. Create student list and create endpoints with Django REST Framework. Document request and response examples, include invalid input tests and restrict the list to authorized users. Explain which fields are writable and why.
  5. Build a dashboard using template inheritance and a shared navigation bar. Demonstrate login protection and denied administrator access for a student. Explain the difference between hiding a link and securing its endpoint.
  6. Write dashboard/API access tests and a deployment runbook covering secrets, DEBUG, allowed hosts, database migrations, static files, application server and rollback. Demonstrate the app in a local production-style preview.
course.duration: 6 classes · 18 live hours plus independent practice
course.requirements: Basic computer use, a code editor, a browser and a local development environment. Frontend framework tracks assume basic JavaScript; backend tracks include introductory language review.
course.targetAudience: Learners building their first structured web application; instructors should review prerequisites with the cohort.

class.title: 01. Web requests and Python data modelling
class.objectives: Explain web requests and python data modelling; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A browser sends a request and a Django application decides how to respond. Python data structures help model the records and transformations within that workflow.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Lists preserve an ordered collection, tuples represent fixed sequences, dictionaries map keys to values and sets represent distinct values. Choose a structure based on the required operations. Validate input before calculations and handle an empty collection explicitly. A server must enforce rules even when a browser form has already checked them. Trace a request from URL to view to storage to response so errors can be located at the correct boundary.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

scores = {'Ada': 82, 'Sam': 74, 'Mina': 91}
if scores:
    average = sum(scores.values()) / len(scores)
    best = max(scores, key=scores.get)
    print(round(average, 1), best)

sections.body:

questions.text: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the protocol used for communication between web clients and servers.

questions.text: Which component is primarily responsible for displaying the user interface of a web application?
questions.explanation: The frontend is the part of a web application users interact with in their browser.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is normally used to retrieve data from a server?
questions.explanation: GET requests are generally used to retrieve resources without modifying server data.

questions.text: What does CRUD represent?
questions.explanation: CRUD describes the four basic operations commonly performed on stored data.

questions.text: A Django application needs to store information about registered students. Which component would normally be responsible for persistent storage?
questions.explanation: Databases provide persistent storage for application data such as students, courses, and assignments.

questions.text: A browser sends a request to `/courses/`. Which backend component should generally determine what happens when that URL is requested?
questions.explanation: URL routing maps requested URLs to the appropriate backend view or handler.

questions.text: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
questions.explanation: Python uses the `def` keyword to define functions.

questions.text: Which Python data structure stores key-value pairs?
questions.explanation: A dictionary stores data using keys associated with corresponding values.

questions.text: Which Python collection is ordered and can contain duplicate values?
questions.explanation: Python lists maintain order and allow duplicate elements.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a Python class?

options.text: To define a blueprint for creating objects
To connect directly to a browser

questions.explanation: Classes define attributes and behavior that objects created from the class can have.

class.title: 03. Forms and server-side validation
class.objectives: Explain forms and server-side validation; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A Django form turns untrusted request data into validated values and usable error messages. Rendering a form and accepting its submission are separate steps.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: For a GET request show an unbound form; for POST bind the request data and call is_valid before reading cleaned_data. Keep invalid forms bound so errors and entered values are preserved. Use CSRF protection for session-authenticated state-changing browser requests. A ModelForm must explicitly restrict editable fields rather than exposing privileged fields unintentionally. Redirect after a successful POST to reduce accidental repeat submissions.

    email = forms.EmailField()

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of a Django Form?
questions.explanation: Django Forms provide tools for rendering, validating, and processing user-submitted data.

questions.text: What is a `ModelForm`?

options.text: A form automatically generated from a Django model

questions.explanation: `ModelForm` simplifies form creation by generating form fields based on a Django model.

questions.text: Why should data submitted through a form be validated?

options.text: To ensure the submitted data meets expected rules

questions.explanation: Validation helps ensure submitted data is complete, correctly formatted, and acceptable to the application.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is normally used when submitting a form that changes server-side data?
questions.explanation: POST is commonly used for operations that submit or modify data on the server.

questions.text: What security mechanism does Django commonly use to protect POST forms against CSRF attacks?
questions.explanation: Django's CSRF protection uses a token to help ensure that POST requests originate from trusted pages.

questions.text: A registration form requires an email address. The user submits the form without one. What should Django ideally do?

options.text: Validate the input and display an appropriate error

questions.explanation: Form validation should identify invalid or missing required data and return useful feedback to the user.

questions.text: When should a bound Django form expose values through cleaned_data for processing?
questions.explanation: Successful validation produces cleaned values suitable for the next operation.

questions.text: An invalid form POST should normally render which form?

options.text: A new blank form with no errors
The bound form with errors and entered values

questions.explanation: A bound form preserves input and validation feedback.

questions.text: Why explicitly list editable ModelForm fields?

options.text: To prevent unintended editing of privileged fields

questions.explanation: An explicit allowlist avoids exposing fields such as roles unintentionally.

questions.text: Why redirect after a successful form POST?

options.text: To make every request a POST
To reduce accidental repeat submission on refresh

questions.explanation: The subsequent page refresh repeats a GET rather than the original POST.

class.title: 04. REST APIs and serializers
class.objectives: Explain rest apis and serializers; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: An API exposes a structured contract for another client, such as React or a mobile application. A serializer controls how data is validated and represented.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Use explicit serializer fields and validate incoming data before saving. Keep list and create behavior predictable with documented status codes. JSON encoding does not perform authorization: views must enforce permissions and scope querysets to allowed records. Use pagination for growing lists. Mark server-owned fields read-only and avoid exposing password hashes or private internal metadata. Test malformed input and missing records alongside successful requests.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

from rest_framework import serializers
class StudentSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Student
        fields = ['id', 'name', 'email', 'student_code']
        read_only_fields = ['id']

questions.text: What is the purpose of a serializer in Django REST Framework?

options.text: Convert complex data such as model instances into representations such as JSON and validate input

questions.explanation: Serializers convert data between Python/model objects and representations such as JSON while also supporting validation.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is typically used to create a new resource through an API?
questions.explanation: POST is commonly used to submit data that creates a new resource.

questions.text: Which HTTP status code generally indicates that a resource was successfully retrieved?
questions.explanation: HTTP 200 OK generally indicates that the request was successfully processed.

questions.text: A mobile application needs to retrieve a student's course list from Django. What would normally provide this data?

questions.text: An API receives a request containing invalid student registration data. What should the API generally return?

options.text: Appropriate validation errors and an error status code

questions.explanation: APIs should validate incoming data and provide useful error responses rather than accepting invalid information.

questions.text: Which serializer field should generally be read-only when the server creates it?
questions.explanation: The client should not assign a server-owned generated identifier.

questions.text: Does serializing a private record to JSON authorize its release?

options.text: Yes, if the response is small
No, permissions and queryset scoping are still required

questions.explanation: Representation and access control solve different problems.

questions.text: What should a growing student-list API support?
questions.explanation: Pagination limits response size and work per request.

questions.text: What should an API do with invalid create data?

options.text: Return validation errors without saving the invalid record

questions.explanation: Validation must precede persistence of the requested changes.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A dashboard combines identity, permissions and presentation. Reusable templates reduce duplicated markup, while authorization controls which records reach the template.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Use Django’s authentication facilities and protect the dashboard with a login requirement. Check permissions separately for administrator actions. Scope student queries to the authenticated account rather than accepting ownership from a query parameter. Put shared navigation in a base template and pass view data through context. Templates escape ordinary values by default; avoid marking untrusted content safe. Keep static assets distinct from private uploaded documents.

sections.title: Worked demonstration

Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.shortcuts import render
@login_required
def dashboard(request):
    return render(request, 'students/dashboard.html', {'student_name': request.user.get_username()})

questions.text: What is authentication?

options.text: Determining what a user is allowed to do

questions.explanation: Authentication verifies that a user is who they claim to be.

questions.text: What is authorization?

options.text: Determining what an authenticated user is permitted to access

questions.explanation: Authorization determines what actions or resources a user is allowed to access.

questions.text: Which Django component provides built-in functionality for managing users and authentication?
questions.explanation: Django includes a built-in authentication system for users, passwords, groups, permissions, login, and logout.

questions.text: Why should user passwords never be stored as plain text?

options.text: SQL databases do not support passwords
Plain-text passwords can be exposed directly if the database is compromised

questions.explanation: Passwords should be securely hashed so that a database breach does not directly expose users' passwords.

questions.text: A student is logged in but attempts to access an administrator-only page. What should happen?

options.text: The student should automatically become an administrator
The student should receive the admin password

questions.explanation: Authentication alone does not grant permission to perform every action. Authorization must be enforced.

questions.text: What is a good way to implement different access levels such as Student, Instructor, and Admin?

options.text: Hide admin links only with JavaScript

questions.explanation: Roles, groups, and permissions provide a structured way to control access to application functionality.

questions.text: Which Django feature is primarily used to generate dynamic HTML pages?
questions.explanation: Django templates allow HTML pages to include dynamic data and logic provided by views.

questions.text: What is template inheritance used for?

options.text: Reusing common HTML layouts across multiple pages

questions.explanation: Template inheritance allows pages to share common structures such as headers, navigation, and footers.

questions.text: What does the Django template expression `{{ student.name }}` generally do?
questions.explanation: Double curly braces are used to output values from the template context.

questions.text: What is Django's static files system used for?

options.text: Managing files such as CSS, JavaScript, and frontend images

questions.explanation: Static files include assets such as CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and images used by the frontend.

class.title: 06. Security tests and production operations
class.objectives: Explain security tests and production operations; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A production Django application needs explicit configuration and repeatable checks. A development server and a successful homepage request are insufficient evidence of readiness.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Test authenticated and anonymous responses, invalid form submissions and cross-account access. Use a disposable database for tests. Disable DEBUG in production, configure allowed hosts, protect secrets and use an appropriate application server behind HTTPS. Plan database migrations and backups, collect static assets and restrict access to private uploads. Examine errors through controlled logs rather than exposing debugging pages to visitors. Verify the deployment configuration before switching traffic.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

from django.test import TestCase
class DashboardAccessTests(TestCase):
    def test_anonymous_user_is_redirected(self):
        response = self.client.get('/dashboard/')
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)

sections.title: Guided practical exercise
sections.body:
Write dashboard/API access tests and a deployment runbook covering secrets, DEBUG, allowed hosts, database migrations, static files, application server and rollback. Demonstrate the app in a local production-style preview.

Work in a disposable project using synthetic student data. Record expected behavior before running it. Compare the result with your prediction and explain one mistake you corrected.

sections.body: Explain the input, transformation and output of your solution. Identify one boundary where data can fail or access must be checked. Describe the evidence that your solution handles that boundary. Return to the concepts above if you cannot explain your code without reading it aloud.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of automated testing?

options.text: To identify defects and verify expected behavior

questions.explanation: Automated tests help verify that application behavior matches expectations and can detect regressions.

questions.text: Which Django class is commonly used as a base for tests that require Django's testing features and database support?
questions.explanation: Django's `TestCase` provides a convenient foundation for testing Django applications, including database interactions.

questions.text: What type of attack attempts to inject malicious SQL into an application's database queries?
questions.explanation: SQL injection occurs when attackers manipulate database queries through unsafe handling of input.

questions.text: What does XSS stand for?
questions.explanation: Cross-Site Scripting involves injecting malicious scripts into content that is delivered to users.

questions.text: Why should `DEBUG` generally be set to `False` in a production Django deployment?

options.text: To prevent users from logging in
To avoid exposing sensitive debugging information

questions.explanation: Production applications should not expose detailed debugging information because it can reveal sensitive implementation details.

questions.text: A Django application is deployed publicly, but its `SECRET_KEY` is stored directly in source code on GitHub. What is the best response?

options.text: Put the secret in a CSS file
Leave it there because GitHub is secure
Rotate the exposed secret and move secrets to secure environment/configuration storage

questions.explanation: Sensitive secrets should not be committed to source control. An exposed secret should be rotated and replaced with securely managed configuration.

questions.text: What does deployment mean in web development?

options.text: Making an application available in a target environment for users

questions.explanation: Deployment involves making the application available on infrastructure where users or other systems can access it.

questions.text: Which server is commonly used to serve a Django application through the WSGI interface in production?
questions.explanation: Gunicorn is a commonly used Python WSGI application server for deploying Django applications.

questions.text: Why are environment variables commonly used in production Django applications?

options.text: To store configuration and sensitive values outside source code

questions.explanation: Environment variables can hold values such as database credentials, secret keys, API keys, and environment-specific configuration.

questions.text: What command is commonly used to apply existing Django migrations to the database?
questions.explanation: `migrate` applies migration files to the configured database. `makemigrations` creates migration files from model changes.
